_note: Forecast versions, oldest first. `from` = when it went live (ISO, UTC; the time the deploy was finished, as in scripts/accuracy-snapshot.mjs). `what` = one plain sentence for /forecast-accuracy (si/ta in lib/i18n/forecastKpi.ts, keyed by id). Optional `modelVersion` = a regex the run's stored model_version must match (every run so far carries the same coefficient date, so none is set). A run belongs to the latest version whose `from` is not after its issue time. Add an entry when a candidate is promoted (DOCS.md "Forecast KPIs").

versions.name: First forecast
versions.what: The first forecasts: a rain-based model for the next hours, and a simple trend line for gauges without a model.

versions.name: Gauge-only model
versions.what: The next 1, 3 and 6 hours now come from the river's own recent movement (fitted on 11 months of readings) instead of extending the trend.

versions.name: Storm model v3
versions.what: Heavy rain over the catchment now lifts the 12 and 24 hour forecasts, and the stated range widens when a storm is under way.

versions.name: Storm model v4
versions.what: In storms the forecast reads the rain the satellite actually measured, timing rain beside the gauge and rain upstream separately.

versions.name: Sensor-glitch filter
versions.what: One-reading spikes and frozen sensors are cleaned out of the readings the forecast learns from, so a faulty gauge no longer distorts it.

versions.name: Rising when the river just rose
versions.what: When a river has just risen 3 cm or more in the last hour, the "Next hour" line says Rising even if the forecast had expected it to hold, so fast rises are not missed.
